messages.text: Great, the first round of review-comments ar on PR #4 - look at those and discuss as a team the options, where possible answer, or adapt the plan.

I’ll read the PR comments, ask the relevant specialists to assess the options, and update the proposal where the feedback supports a concrete change. I’ll also reply on the PR with the team’s conclusions and any decisions that still need your input.

The review gives us clearer targets: tracker coverage to |η| < 4, calorimetry to |η| < 5, and muons to |η| < 3 with 3.5 as a stretch goal.

The team found two important consequences. A separate forward calorimeter can fit beyond the present muon envelope, but it cannot absorb hadrons before they reach those muon stations. Also, a finite-solenoid estimate gives substantially less field near the tracker ends than at its centre. Both need to shape the next proposal.

The revised drawing now includes a proposed forward calorimeter at |z| = 11.2–13.2 m, plus smaller endcap apertures to study muon coverage to |η| = 3.5. The team also recommends studying separate barrel and forward timing assemblies; timing cannot be assumed from an ordinary outer silicon layer.

I’m keeping the magnet alternatives open as requested. The proposal now treats standalone-compatible, potentially toroidal muon detection as the baseline investigation, and schedules punch-through studies before any decision to add absorber steel.

All 25 comments now have a documented response: a change, a sourced answer, or an explicit deferral. The updated prototype passes 11 tests and checks 21 directions, distinguishing a full axial traversal from a grazing intersection.

The literature cross-check also found conflicting published CMS forward-calorimeter radii. I’ve preserved that discrepancy rather than choosing one silently; the proposed nODD dimensions remain independent choices. I’m finishing the checks before pushing the revision and replying in the review threads.

The revised proposal is pushed to [PR #4](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/4), and all 25 review threads now have team replies. The main choices for the next review are forward-calorimeter placement and its support/shielding envelope, beam-line clearance for the smaller apertures, and the timing/services allocation. Thread resolution and design sign-off remain with the human reviewer.

Updated [PR #4](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/4) after team discussion and replied to **all 25 comments**.

Key changes:

- Revised envelopes and r–z drawing with dedicated forward calorimetry.
- Adopted the requested coverage objectives.
- Added sourced assessments of magnets, timing, services and minimum tracker radius.
- Added a validation-study catalogue; preserved explicitly deferred decisions.

**Validation:** 33 tests passed; 23 session records validated. No detector simulation or design sign-off claimed.

The proposal remains draft. Main open questions concern forward shielding/supports, beam-line clearance, and timing/service space. Working tree clean.
